Source page: Network Fundamentals, 6 weeks, instructor notes. Week 1 Introduction. Scope of the course, how the layers of the TCP/IP model map onto the OSI model, and a short history of packet switching from ARPANET to the modern internet. Students install a packet capture tool and record their first ping. Week 2 Link layer and addressing. Ethernet framing, MAC addresses, ARP resolution and the ARP cache, VLAN tags, and a lab in which trainees read frames from a switch mirror port. Week 3 Internet layer. IPv4 addressing and subnetting, CIDR notation, IPv6 addressing basics, ICMP for diagnostics, fragmentation and path MTU discovery. Trainees subnet a /22 block by hand. Week 4 Transport layer. TCP connection setup and teardown, the three-way handshake, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, flow control with the sliding window, and UDP for connectionless delivery. Week 5 Congestion and reliability. Slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit and fast recovery, retransmission timers from round-trip estimates, and a lab that plots the congestion window. Week 6 Application layer and wrap up. DNS resolution and caching, HTTP request and response flow, TLS handshake overview, and a final capture exercise that trainees present to the group. Assessment: two labs and a final capture report.
